translationRepairs: After successive appointments as magistrate of Xia County, he became known for administrative ability.
Through successive appointments he became magistrate of Xia County and became known for administrative ability.
累授夏縣令 is successive promotion culminating in the Xia magistracy, not repeated tenure as Xia magistrate; the proposed line restores that career shape.

Though I still face court gossip, you have known me from the first as an old colleague and will not heed idle talk. Just as Jia Yi was called back to the privy chamber and Sang Hongyang was trusted again to manage state revenue, I dare not spare myself in repaying your confidence.

Though as a guest at the Eastern Court I still face official slander, you have remained my old friend from first to last and will not heed idle talk. Just as Jia Yi was called back to the privy chamber and Sang Hongyang was trusted again to manage state revenue, I dare not spare myself in repaying your confidence.
晏賓於東朝 and 官謗 are omitted or flattened in the original, and 相公終始故舊 is a first-to-last old friendship; the replacement restores those elements without adding unstated facts.
and the story of Supervisor Li Jie's new embankment, with statues adorned at the River Temple, stern as though living.
and the story of Censor-in-Chief Li Jie's new embankment, with statues adorned at the River Temple, stern as though living.
大夫李傑 is Li Jie’s high censorial title (御史大夫), not an office of Supervisor.

In June 769 he and Right Vice Director Pei Zunqing took up office at the Ministry of Personnel; the emperor ordered extra provisions from the imperial kitchen and allowed Eunuch Yu Chaoen and all regular court officials down to the chancellors to visit the ministry with congratulations.

In the sixth month of Dali 4 (AD 769) he and Right Vice Director Pei Zunqing took up office at the Ministry of Personnel; the emperor ordered extra provisions from the imperial kitchen and allowed Eunuch Yu Chaoen and all regular court officials down to the chancellors to visit the ministry with congratulations.
大歷四年六月 is the sixth lunar month of Dali 4; Gregorian June is not in the source.
In March 777 Chancellor Yuan Zai was executed; Yan was ordered to conduct the interrogation.
In the third month of Dali 12 (AD 777) Chancellor Yuan Zai was executed; Yan was ordered to conduct the interrogation.
十二年三月, following the Dali dating of the surrounding units, is the third lunar month of Dali 12, not Gregorian March.
In December 778 he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
In the twelfth month of Dali 13 (AD 778) he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
十三年十二月 is the twelfth lunar month of Dali 13, not Gregorian December.
Yang meant to avenge Zai, and rumor held that Daizong favored Consort Dugu and loved her son Prince Han Huai; Yan had secretly urged making Dugu empress.
Yang meant to avenge Zai, and rumor held that Daizong favored Consort Dugu and loved her son Jiong, Prince of Han; Yan had secretly urged making Dugu empress.
韓王迥 names Jiong, Prince of Han; Huai mistranslates 迥.
Zhu Ci and Cui Ning also sided with Youfu; Ning spoke sharply; Yang was furious and banished Ning to command the Bin-Fang region to break his spirit.
Zhu Ci and Cui Ning also sided with Youfu; Ning spoke sharply; Yang was furious and banished Ning to command the Fu-Fang region to break his spirit.
鄜坊 is Fu and Fang; Bin would be 邠, which is not in the text.

Zhu Ci and Cui Ning also joined Youfu from the side in mediation; Ning's words were rather sharp; Yang was greatly angered and therefore expelled Ning to command Bin and Fang circuits to break his spirit.

Zhu Ci and Cui Ning also joined Youfu from the side in mediation; Ning's words were rather sharp; Yang was greatly angered and therefore expelled Ning to command Fu and Fang circuits to break his spirit.
The literal likewise reads 鄜 as Bin; Fu and Fang is required.
Yan wished to fabricate crimes against him; knowing Yu Zhun and Yan had long borne a grudge, he recommended Yu as military commissioner of Jingnan to spy on Yan's movements.
Yang Yan wished to fabricate crimes against him; knowing Yu Zhun and Liu Yan had long borne a grudge, he recommended Yu as military commissioner of Jingnan to spy on Liu Yan's movements.
炎欲 is Yang Yan, while later 晏 is Liu Yan; bare Yan for both collides the two men.
In 789, once the emperor realized his error, he recalled Yan's son Zhijing and appointed him director of learning at the Imperial Academy;
In 789, once the emperor realized his error, he took Yan's son Zhijing into service and appointed him erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;
錄 is enrollment into service, not recall, and 太常博士 is an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, not a director at the Imperial Academy; ‘recorded’ is still awkward in idiomatic English.
In the fifth year of Zhenyuan, when the emperor came to understand, he only then recorded Yan's son Zhijing and appointed him as director in the Imperial Academy;
In the fifth year of Zhenyuan, when the emperor came to understand, he only then recorded Yan's son Zhijing and appointed him erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;
The literal already has 錄 as ‘recorded’ but still misrenders 太常博士 as an Imperial Academy directorship.
Early on, finding the treasury short and goods dear while copper coin remained scarce, Qi proposed minting the Qianyuan Heavy Treasure coin, valued at ten ordinary coins each.
Early on, finding the treasury short and coin dear while goods remained cheap, Qi proposed minting the Qianyuan Heavy Treasure coin, valued at ten ordinary coins each.
幣重貨輕 means coin was dear and goods cheap; the original reverses that couplet.
Emperor Xuanzong was greatly pleased; that very day Qi was appointed investigating censor and put in charge of Jiang-Huai land-and-labor tax commissioner.
Emperor Xuanzong was greatly pleased; that very day Qi was appointed investigating censor and put in charge as Jiang-Huai land-and-labor tax commissioner.
勾當江淮租庸使 is appointment as that commissioner; ‘put in charge of’ plus the bare title is ungrammatical, and ‘as’ restores the office.

An Lushan had already overrun five commanderies, including Hejian and Xindu, yet Jinming had won no victories on the field. Furious, Emperor Xuanzong dispatched a eunuch bearing an imperial sword with this ultimatum: "Recover the lost territory, or Helan Jinming loses his head."

An Lushan had already overrun five commanderies, including Hejian and Xindu, yet Jinming had won no victories on the field. Furious, Emperor Xuanzong dispatched a palace envoy bearing an imperial sword with this ultimatum: "Recover the lost territory, or Helan Jinming loses his head."
中使 is a palace envoy; the original’s ‘eunuch’ specifies an identity the sentence does not give.

Zhang Pang had first been on good terms with Hong; Hong recommended him as vice director of agriculture; when Can wished Pang to share management of Jiang-Huai salt-and-iron, he consulted Hong; Hong because Pang was jealous and harsh, fearing he would use law to bind Xu Can, therefore said: "Pang is violent and obstinate, hard to control—not usable."

Zhang Pang had first been on good terms with Hong; Hong recommended him as vice director of agriculture; when Can wished Pang to share management of Jiang-Huai salt-and-iron, he consulted Hong; Hong, because Pang hated evil and was severe, and fearing he would bind Xu Can with the law, therefore said: "Pang is violent and obstinate, hard to control—not usable."
嫉惡 is hatred of evil, not jealousy; the original reverses why Hong feared Pang would prosecute Xu Can.

Before long Hong spoke to chancellors Zhao Jing and Lu Zhi: "Hong's duty is transport—each year fifty thousand shi of Jiang-Huai rice shipped; the year before last increased to seven hundred thousand shi to fill the Great Storehouse; fortunately without fault.

Before long Hong spoke to chancellors Zhao Jing and Lu Zhi: "Hong's duty is transport—each year five hundred thousand shi of Jiang-Huai rice shipped; the year before last increased to seven hundred thousand shi to fill the Great Storehouse; fortunately without fault.
五十萬斛 is five hundred thousand shi; fifty thousand undercounts by ten.

When Emperor Shunzong came to the throne, Wang Shuwen stripped him of real authority. He was appointed Minister of Military Affairs, then shortly relieved as Acting Minister of Personnel and left in charge as Garrison Commander of the Eastern Capital.

When Emperor Shunzong came to the throne, Wang Shuwen stripped him of real authority. He was appointed Minister of Military Affairs, then shortly appointed Acting Minister of Personnel and Garrison Commander of the Eastern Capital.
尋除檢校吏部尚書、東都留守 is a further appointment to both posts; 除 does not mean relieve.
After a year he was summoned as Supervising Censor, sent out as Hunan Observation Commissioner; he was keen on governance.
After a year he was summoned as Supervising Secretary, sent out as Hunan Observation Commissioner; he was keen on governance.
給事中 is a Chancellery supervising secretary, not a censor.
Grand Mentor Du You headed the finance, salt, iron, and transport commission. Impressed by Li Xun's administrative skill, he recommended him as deputy commissioner.
Situ Du You headed the finance, salt, iron, and transport commission. Impressed by Li Xun's administrative skill, he recommended him as deputy commissioner.
司徒 is Situ, not Grand Mentor (太傅).
Duke Du You presided over finance, salt, iron, and transport; because Xun was capable in administration, he memorialized him as vice commissioner.
Situ Du You presided over finance, salt, iron, and transport; because Xun was capable in administration, he memorialized him as vice commissioner.
司徒 is Situ, not a ducal title.
After a long time, Xun went from Supervising Censor to Hunan Observation Commissioner—Chenzhou was precisely a subordinate prefecture.
After a long time, Xun went from Supervising Secretary to Hunan Observation Commissioner—Chenzhou was precisely a subordinate prefecture.
給事中 is again a supervising secretary, not a censor.
